quest.title: A Certain Notice
quest.description: Iaune from the Maison Gestion is hard at work...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: ...I just can't believe it. Would someone really take a Kamera into the Maison Gestion itself, and simply strut about taking pictures of everyone and anything?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: It is ridiculous! Everyone knows, everyone should know, that that is how secrets get leaked! It is common sense!

dialogues.speaker: Roialte
dialogues.text: If common sense was common, Mr. Iaune, then the Maison Gestion could simply disband tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Roialte
dialogues.text: I shall leave this to you. Have them sign the document, just like I taught you, and return it to me before the weekend.

dialogues.speaker: Roialte
dialogues.text: I still have to handle the expense receipts. Carsix keeps hassling me about it.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: But, Mr. Roialte, just who should I be looking for? We don't have an office specifically in charge of Kameras.

dialogues.speaker: Roialte
dialogues.text: Uh... I trust your judgment. Now hurry up and take care of this, so we can each really enjoy the weekend! I'm going to go take care of other things. Hop to it, kid!

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Yessir, Mr. Roialte.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Roialte leaves in a leisurely manner...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Huh? Hello, hello. It looks, though, you are not a member of the staff here at the Maison Gestion.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: I am currently busy with official business. Should you have any inquiries, please ask Ms. Cornelia. She's right over there.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: She will provide you with a chair and a cup of tea. Please have a seat, and I will come find you after I am done.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the big rush?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's... It's actually a simple matter, but dealing with it is quite complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: The office I work in has received a notice instructing us to draft a letter to the other offices.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: The content was something like, staff are forbidden from bringing Kameras into the Maison Gestion and taking pictures, except for work purposes, in order to avoid leakage of secret information.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Does telling me about the letter's contents constitute leaking secrets?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: No, certainly not. If anyone really had used a Kamera to take a photo of documents, and it resulted in a leak, then this would certainly be a confidential matter.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: However, "maybe someone will use a Kamera to take a picture of documents in order to leak them" is not a secret. After all, that's a possibility that everyone is aware of.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Think about it this way: If you are guarding a secret, then the secret you are guarding certainly cannot be revealed.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: But the fact that "you are guarding a secret" itself may not be considered secret.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: After all, if even the fact that "you are guarding a secret" is considered a secret, then you will fall into an endless cycle of keeping the secret of keeping secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your wording is an endless cycle!

choices.text: I'm curious who is in charge of this matter...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: That is where this matter becomes complicated. There is no office in the entire Maison Gestion that is directly charged with managing Kameras.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Mr. Semaine says that I should ask Mr. Gattineo. Their work is related to confidential matters, and thus they should be the first to be made aware.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But Mr. Roialte says that I should ask Difor, as he is in charge of all matters related to the staff of the Maison Gestion.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Were we to make a new rule that all staff of the Maison Gestion cannot bring Kameras to work, we'd have to let them know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... That's complicated... Why are there so many different people responsible for different things? What happens if you can't remember?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: That's why each of us carries a thick notepad. Though even with the notes, I'm still not sure who I should look for now...

choices.text: Then who is responsible for this?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Well, I guess you'll get to see for yourselves. Please, this way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a confidential matter. Let's look for Gattineo.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: That's exactly what I thought. Mr. Gattineo is quite affable, and is also an "exemplary Gestionnaire."

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Even though all the matters he deals with are of utmost importance, he still handles each matter with aplomb. His work can truly be called outstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a matter involving personnel. Let's look for Difor.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: That's exactly what I thought, but he has quite the explosive temper, and though he is quite reliable, his sharp tongue is sure to leave a mark.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: *sigh* But he must be informed of this matter as soon as possible...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Iaune! What're the odds? Do you finally have time for a cup of coffee with me after work?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Thank you for your offer, but I have a confidential matter that requires your attention.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: "Confidential matter"? Is it something I know about?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: I think you may not have been informed yet. I only received the document this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Now that's odd. Perhaps my information is a step behind yours since I haven't had a chance to read The Steambird yet today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's a confidential matter. Why would you read about it in The Steambird?

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Those reporters get information and spread it far faster than our internal memos here at the Maison Gestion can.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Of course, it's understandable. After all, they get paid when they deliver a message.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it at all...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Let's not talk about that for now. Sir, it's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Ha! That's right, such an announcement is absolutely necessary. This already happened. Some blithering idiot wanted to show off his desk layout, and took a picture of it.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: He's a member of the Kamera Club, and showed that very photo to the other members of the club.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: But one of the members of said club just happened to be an astute reporter, who quickly noticed a document that looked like an internal memo in the picture.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: And guess what happened next? The next day, that blasted memo complaining that only fish gets served for dinner here, day in and day out, was all over The Steambird!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that count as a secret...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound very serious...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Whatever it is, it's internal information, and it should not be leaked to any outside parties!

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: The people of the Court of Fontaine never miss an opportunity to mock and deride the Maison Gestion, and we must act with caution.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: As if they actually gave two figs about what we actually do here! All they want to do is... ugh, have a laugh.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Uh, anyway... I'll leave this to your office to take care of, then...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: But this matter concerns new rules for personnel... Difor is the one who should sign off on this.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: After all, in this document, though it reminds everyone of the importance of keeping confidential information secret, the more important thing is how to communicate these principles to them.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: If you ask me, it must be Difor that takes care of this. Our office will certainly assist in this matter. This will be more efficient, and confidentiality can be maintained.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Gattineo swiftly signs his name on the dotted line reading "co-organizer"...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: But, Mr. Gattineo! This matter...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Come on, boy! You can't dawdle about, this must be taken care of! Now go find Difor quickly, before his patience is worn thin by other matters.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Now, I'll go find some documents that talk about the principles of protecting secret information. When the document is ready to be officially promulgated, our office will provide our full support!

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Go find him, kid! I've got to go... uh, attend to other matters.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Gattineo strides off...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: What? Mr. Gattineo! Wait!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: There, did you see Mr. Gattineo's abilities? His secret to getting everything done so well is avoiding doing anything at all that carries even a modicum of risk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it's the ability to shirk your duties...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: There's nothing we can do now... Except go find Mr. Difor. This way, please.

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Do you have something for me, Iaune? You seem to be out of breath.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: It's like this, Mr. Difor...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: You've come to the wrong person, Iaune. This document clearly has the subject of "secrets." How could you fail to realize something so simple and obvious?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: I thought the subject was "this document."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Grammatically speaking, that's correct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, that's not the subject right now, either!

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Your exactness is noted and appreciated. But I will not sign this document no matter what. I will not even entertain the thought! It should be Gattineo who leads this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Mr. Gattineo said, you should be the one in charge...

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Ha! ME? And how should I do it? Grab a megaphone and stand at the door, shouting at everyone as they come in to work?

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: "Hey! Ladies and Gentlemen, don't bring your Kameras to work! You'll leak all kinds of secrets! That would be bad, so don't!"

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Or maybe print up a few hundred documents, and leave them on the desk of every Gestionnaire so they can take them with them as they go get their coffee?

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: You think we're like Gattineo? That we can just grab leakers and teach them a lesson? All we can do is send out notices, the kind nobody takes notice of!

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: But, he's already signed the document, look here...

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Boy, do you have any clue what "co-organizer" means?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Um... the one who follows instructions from the other party?

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: It means "At least I'm not responsible for this."

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: I categorically and completely refuse to sign this document. If it must be my office that is forced to take charge of this, then let Maneval come down and tell me so in person!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Difor charges out in a rage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—He's so loud... Paimon didn't even dare to speak...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: As I said, he has quite the temper.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what do we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Don't worry, let's just go back and look for Mr. Roialte.

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Iaune! Let me guess. Bad news?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Sir, you are correct it is not good news. To be precise, it is "secret" news.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So it is.

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Very funny, Iaune. So what is this "secret" news?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: That is true, something like this could easily happen. After all, most of the staff here at the Maison Gestion aren't very sensitive to how confidential different documents are.

choices.text: Do people really ignore something that serious?

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: It's all thanks to Gattineo and his people. All the documents here have to be reviewed by them. They decide the security classification of the document and stamp it.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Sounds like a good system, right? But the folks in charge of reviewing documents came up with a truly ingenious way to save time: just stamp "secret" on every single blasted document that comes their way!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Last week, Carsix went to the Opera Epiclese for a speech, and talked about recent performances.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I remember, it wasn't a long speech, and lots of people were there. The text of his speech was even in the newspapers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since the speech was given in front of everyone, and everyone knows it all already... how can something everyone knows be a secret?

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: But noooo, even so, Gattineo still just has to classify it as "secret."

choices.text: Maybe there was some important information inside it?

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: AS IF! He classified the draft that had already been presented to the public as "secret," but didn't bother with any of the previous versions!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Carsix never writes his own speeches! The entire text of every draft is written for him by someone else!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: The only changes he makes to the entire speech are to sign his name and change a few irrelevant adjectives!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: And all those older manuscripts that he didn't edit? Of course they're lying on Carsix's desk, nobody cares!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: If Gattineo actually cared one iota about protecting secrets, why doesn't he classify those as secret too?

choices.text: This could be another way of protecting secrets.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Oh, come on! They just want to save time. To Gattineo, the best way to protect secrets is to make absolutely every trivial little thing a secret.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: That way, nobody knows what the actual secrets that need protecting are. Not even them!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: If you want to hide a glass of water, the best way is to dump it in a lake! Great plan, nothing can ever go wrong!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: And if you want to hide a glass of Fonta? Are you going to turn the whole lake into a lake of Fonta?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #A lake of Fonta... hehehe, Paimon wants to go swim in it! Fonta's really tasty, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: So... This document...

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Iaune, this matter does concern personnel, so you've come to the right person.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: But first, you must let Gattineo ascertain the security classification. Just like I said before...

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Before we can officially begin our work, we must know if it's a glass of water or a glass of Fonta we're hiding.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: As we're already old colleagues, I won't cause any trouble for you. Our office will absolutely support and assist with this matter...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Difor slowly looks over the file, and lazily scrawls his name on the dotted line reading "co-organizer"...

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Very well! Now, go find Gattineo! This will affect all the staff, so I must go and inform the relevant people in advance...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But, Mr. Difor...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Difor walks off without looking back...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: *sigh* That's Mr. Difor for you, quick to anger but quite clever...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Nothing we can do now but look for Gattineo. This way, please.

choices.text: We'll go get some for you in a bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Then it's a deal! No backsies!

choices.text: Uh... Maybe he has a good reason...
Did nobody tell them about the "security classification" system?

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Iaune! To think I'd meet you here, you little rascal.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Mr. Gattineo, I was just looking for you! There's something you should know...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: What is it? I just finished reading today's Steambird, and the Maison Gestion wasn't mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Yes, this is a secret matter.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Oh, now that's a rare sight! Someone besides a journalist who can tell if something is secret or not.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: *sigh* It appears our Difor is an exceptionally diligent journalist. It's almost as if he charged into my office demanding to know the security classification of this document.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: I completely concur with his opinion. This matter certainly must be reviewed and classified first, but the matter of "Kamera Security Leaks" is quite large, and concerns the entire Maison Gestion.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: My office alone cannot ascertain the confidentiality. I must go to the other offices first, and allow them to review it, and once they are all familiar with the matter, we then can proceed. For example... Carsix.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Huh? But this order came down from Mr. Carsix...

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Then it is even more imperative that he be aware of how we are dealing with it. Come on, lad, let's go find Roialte, and then meet with Carsix.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait! Mr. Gattineo!

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: This is a confidential matter. As such, it falls under your office's jurisdiction.

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Well, in that case, can we keep affairs we handle confidential from you in the future — even on personnel-related matters?

dialogues.speaker: Difor
dialogues.text: Hey, those are two different things. Quit shifting the goalposts!

dialogues.speaker: Gattineo
dialogues.text: Well, it's certainly not up to us to decide whether or not they're the same thing!

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: It looks like... I've messed things up again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, how... How about we get out of here? Adults arguing is scary...

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Gentlemen, gentlemen! Calm down! There's no need to be upset over such a trifling matter!

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: This is no trifling matter, Roialte! This is a matter of grave importance that impacts the entire Maison Gestion. I dare not act rashly and decide it on my own!

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: So it is! There is nothing trivial at all about protecting our secrets. I don't think there is anyone in the whole Maison Gestion more suited to handling this matter than you!

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Please, relax! Why must you gentlemen argue about who is in charge? As I see it, there's no need for anyone to be primarily responsible, you don't even need to coordinate.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: I fear I do not understand your meaning, Roialte.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: I don't quite follow your train of thought, Roialte.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: You two are both gentlemen with a wealth of experience, and know that when dealing with something complicated, we must first divide it into simple things.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: The responsibility of preventing people from leaking secrets using Kameras should logically fall to Gattineo.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: But you need not do anything extra. Just continue catching leakers, as before.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: As for informing everyone of the policy that Kameras can't be brought into Maison Gestion, this troubling task must fall to Difor. Nobody else in the Maison Gestion can clarify the new policy to the staff.

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: We have no capability to enforce it! Nobody listens to us!

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: *sigh* You don't need to worry about that. Leave enforcement to Gattineo, what you need to do is not "notify," but "propose."

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: The bigger you print the proposal, the better. Put it at the entrance, and be sure to print the case of the last Kamera leak below it. That should be enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The sounds exactly like before...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I... I don't understand, Mr. Roialte, this way...

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: I agree with this proposal. Excellent, it's very clean and clear.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Wh—What?

response.speaker: Difor
response.text: Proposal? Ha, that's easy.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Then we have reached an accord. After Iaune rewrites the draft, I'll bring it to both of you to look over. Now... let's each get back to work.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Gattineo and Difor look at each other for a moment, and then each turns and leaves...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I am very sorry, Mr. Roialte, I really messed this up.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Don't blame yourself, Iaune. It's not your fault. At least not completely.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why did they suddenly accept your idea?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I don't get it... I don't get it at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Why did they suddenly stop arguing? They looked like they were about to start a brawl...

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: That's because you don't know what those two gentlemen truly care about. Do you think they simply didn't want to take on extra work?

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Of course not. They simply didn't want any other offices to get involved with their work, especially when they themselves would be held responsible.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: As long as you understand this, it's easy to remove the source of their discontent. And then they are quite willing to do the work.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But... Your proposal, they still have to take responsibility.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Gattineo and Difor are both experienced bureaucrats, and they are both painfully aware of some simple truth...

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: In a large organization such as the Maison Gestion, everyone has to take some responsibility. That's the only way to make sure everything can continue to operate smoothly.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: You can negotiate the size of the responsibility, but everyone must take part. If anyone refuses to do so... Well, then they had best pray they never run into any trouble.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Don't think too much on it, Iaune. You'll come to understand all this someday. Right now, the important thing is to go rewrite a proposal, and bring it to me. Got it?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Yes, Mr. Roialte...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Roialte leaves in a hurry...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Eh, looks like another all-nighter. Guess I should grab a coffee first...

choices.text: Do you always stay up so late?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I wouldn't say "always," but I guess I'm just... used to it.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Regardless, it's all good as long as I get my work done...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: *sigh* Sometimes I wonder if there's a point to all this work I do.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I type, produce documents, chat, and run errands — day in, day out.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: #As an... objective observer, {NICKNAME}, what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Fine. Perhaps you can give me an answer after you've observed a bit more.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: If you're interested, come here tomorrow — we can talk again then.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: As a Gestionnaire here at the Maison Gestion, I've been... drowning in a sea of work.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Perhaps you could tell me, as an objective observer... What's the point of it all?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I know that, but... Forget it. No buts.

choices.text: How is this different from before?
